Committee: Ways and Means General Fund
Sponsor: Pettus
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 02/01/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 81 as introduced allows hazardous duty time to be used in calculating the requisite years of service for inservice death benefits for firefighter, law enforcement, and correctional officer members of the Employees Retirement System and Teacher Retirement System even if the member has not otherwise attained 25 years of creditable service. According to the actuaries for the Retirement Systems of Alabama (RSA), this bill will not increase the state employer contribution rate but could increase the contribution rates of local government employers by an undetermined amount.
Steve Clouse, Chair
Ways and Means General Fund

FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 81 as passed the House of Representatives allows hazardous duty time to be used in calculating the requisite years of service for inservice death benefits for firefighter, law enforcement, and correctional officer members of the Employees Retirement System and Teacher Retirement System even if the member has not otherwise attained 25 years of creditable service. According to the actuaries for the Retirement Systems of Alabama (RSA), this bill will not increase the state employer contribution rate but could increase the contribution rates of local government employers by an undetermined amount.
Greg Albritton, Chairperson
Finance and Taxation General Fund
